_comment_hyperparams: Every combination of values below is run: each mode in 'modes' gets its own full cross-product over ITS hyperparams (rag_hyperparams for rag, agentic_hyperparams for agentic — the two are never combined with each other), and that in turn is cross-produced with model_hyperparams and extraction_hyperparams. Each extra value in ANY list multiplies the total run count — prefer varying one or two dimensions at a time. Omit a key entirely to leave that setting at whatever chatbot/config.json (or extraction/config.json) already has (chatbot.py/process_docs.py only override what's explicitly passed).
_comment_rag_hyperparams: Full list: k_standard, k_deep_dive, top_n, temperature, max_tokens, reranker_enabled, reranker_model, reranker_type, deep_dive, hyde_enabled, bm25_enabled, title_boost_enabled, k_retrieve, deep_dive_batch_size, expansion_char_budget. k_standard/k_deep_dive replace a single 'k' override — chatbot.py --k still exists for a flat override, but each RUN here is either deep_dive or not, so only the matching one of k_standard/k_deep_dive actually takes effect per run (see chatbot/core/rag_chatbot.py). k_retrieve is ignored in deep dive mode; deep_dive_batch_size only applies when deep_dive is true. reranker_model and reranker_type only have an effect when reranker_enabled is true. reranker_type is 'cross_encoder' (default) or 'late_interaction' (ColBERT-style MaxSim via sentence_transformers.MultiVectorEncoder, requires sentence-transformers >= 6.0) — e.g. to A/B the two: reranker_type: ["cross_encoder", "late_interaction"], reranker_model: ["BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3"] paired with a second sweep run overriding reranker_model to "answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1" for the late_interaction leg, since this cross-product can't pair specific model values to specific types.
_comment_agentic_hyperparams: Full list: temperature, max_tokens, max_steps (the agent step budget), max_chars_per_page.
_comment_model_hyperparams: Applied on top of EVERY mode/hyperparameter combination above (the answering LLM choice is independent of rag vs agentic). Full fields: model, base_url, api_key. A single value (as shipped) costs nothing extra — it's the same as chatbot/config.json's own llm.model, just made explicit. Add a second value, e.g. ["mistralai-small", "gpt-4o-mini"], to actually compare two models on the same endpoint. Varying base_url/api_key means switching provider entirely — since values are cross-produced independently, mixing multiple (base_url, api_key) pairs with multiple 'model' values can pair a model name with the wrong endpoint's key; keep base_url/api_key to a single value each (or run separate benchmarks per provider) unless you're sure every combination is valid. Leave as {} to skip this dimension entirely and always use chatbot/config.json's llm block unchanged.
_comment_extraction_hyperparams: Applied on top of EVERY mode/model/hyperparameter combination above. Full fields: use_token_chunking, chunking.max_tokens, chunking.overlap_tokens, chunking.char_chunk_size, chunking.char_overlap, quality.min_score, quality.min_word_count, quality.substantial_word_count, embedding.model, embedding.type, embedding.base_url, embedding.api_key. Shipped empty ON PURPOSE, unlike model_hyperparams above: extraction_cache.get_or_build() has no way to know a value 'already matches' your current extraction/config.json build, so EVEN a single value here — e.g. {"embedding.model": ["all-MiniLM-L6-v2"]}, even if that's already your default — forces one real corpus re-extraction (minutes, no early-exit) the first time this exact combination is seen, before the first run. Each distinct combination costs that once, then is cached under evaluator/extraction_cache/ and reused across every mode/model/hyperparameter combination that shares it (built once, not once per run) — but grid search here runs EVERY combination (no smart sampling like evaluator/optimizer's Bayesian search), so keep this to 1-2 values per field once you do enable it, e.g. {"chunking.char_chunk_size": [800, 1200]} to compare two chunk sizes.
